other_problems: Non-merge files were changed during the merge and are left uncommitted. MERGE_HEAD was written at 02:09:56; these changes came after it: website/joins.py (+6/-2 at 02:28:42, adds zones_before handling to the fixture cut; HEAD's joins.py has none); tests/test_hail_workflow.py (+7/-2 at 02:38:29, moves the end of the B5 clock check to the inserted B3 steps); website/data/hail-fixture/hail/j/r0079_c0198.json, j/r0079_c0199.json and j/r0092_c0214.json (each gains station_candidates and zones_before at 02:28:56); and untracked website/data/hail-fixture/hail/z/MTZ050.json (83 bytes, zone 'Judith Basin', produced only by the joins.py edit). git status --short shows 85 entries, and six of them are not merge files. The fixture's joins parts depend on uncommitted joins.py code, so the merge commit would not reproduce them unless joins.py is committed too. The supervisor must decide, before committing, whether these belong in the merge (they are B5 files) or should be reverted and the fixture rebuilt.

The fixture check fails as written. The literal command 'python -m website.hail fixture <dir>' is rejected because the CLI takes --out DIR, and hail/a needs --addresses-from. With '--out <scratch> --addresses-from /home/user/hail-b5/out/combined/store', the fresh output differs from the working tree in: index.json (the working tree adds a joins block: built_at 2026-10-20T01:24:00Z, zone_list_before ['MTZ050'], zones_before, zone_names with MTZ050); manifest.json (a joins key and entries for j/, k/, s/, z/); and four folders only the working tree has: j/ (8 files), k/ (2), s/ (4), z/ (5). hail/a/ (51 files), hail/t/ (3 files), the index's addresses block and every other index key are identical. Without --addresses-from, hail/a/ and the addresses block are also missing. The working-tree manifest is internally consistent (74 entries, 0 mismatches). fixture_store writes none of the joins parts, and the copy replaces index.json and manifest.json, so D51's 'B5's parts both kept' needs the joins step to regenerate the joins block and its manifest entries. The check must say what it compares.

Unit suite: Ran 1589 tests, FAILED (failures=10, skipped=1). Seven failures are the browser-against-module tests that D51 expects (test_site.HailJoinedRecords: fire-weather zone file, part not loaded, station file not loaded, zone file not loaded (three subtests), browser joins for three cells). The B3 tree passes them, so they fail because HEAD's Python text moved ahead of B3's map.js, as D51 expects. Three failures are not expected: test_site.HailJoinedRecords.test_the_billings_town_page_joins_sit_in_their_sections_newest_first (a Python HTML check; the wind section shows 'Station reading: Data unavailable ...' where the test expects 'Station: Jun 16, 2025: 50 kt (58 mph) at Billings/Logan Intl, about 2.6 miles away'), and test_snowgrid.UrlAndWordsTests.test_no_forbidden_term_in_any_snow_word and test_the_unit_sentence_is_the_plain_sentence_with_no_regression_word (website/snowgrid.py unit_failed ends 'This is not an all-clear.', and the test forbids 'all-clear'). A full run on a git archive of HEAD gives Ran 1264 tests, FAILED (failures=10) with the same ten failing entries, so the merge adds no failure. The three extras are B5 failures already in HEAD; neither snowgrid.py nor test_snowgrid.py is touched by the merge. They still break the brief's 'nothing else may fail' condition.

Budget restatement: tests/test_hail.py (fixture store and joins files under 62,000 bytes, was 50,000) and tests/test_joins.py (62 KB, was 50 KB; measured 60,559 bytes) cite D54 of the brief, which authorises restating budgets to measured sizes. Neither docs/DECISIONS.md nor docs/ROADMAP.md records D54 or the new figure. AGENTS.md says decisions go in DECISIONS.md, so record it at the merge.
